overview: White fianchettoes the kingside bishop against the Sicilian, aiming for a Closed Sicilian set-up with Bg2, Ne2 or Nc3, d3 and f4. After 2...g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 White often plays 4.f4 for a kingside pawn push. Black counterattacks on the queenside with ...Nc6, ...d6, ...Nf6 and ...Rb8/...b5.

white_ideas.idea: Bg2, d3, Nc3/Ne2 and f4, then Nf3 and a kingside pawn advance with f5.
Keep d4 in reserve as a break.

black_ideas.idea: Mirror with ...g6, ...Bg7, ...Nc6, ...d6 and queenside play with ...b5 or ...Rb8.
Strike in the centre with ...d5 when White's pieces are not ready.

typical_structures.structure: Closed Sicilian-type: White f4 and e4 against Black c5 and d6, kingside fianchettoes on both sides.

character.notes: Slow build-up with each side attacking on opposite wings, but few early tactics. Less forcing than the Open Sicilian.

gambit.notes: No material is given in the main line 2...g6.

structure.notes: Asymmetric Sicilian centre; White's e4 against Black's c5 pawn and the c-file. Tension is kept until late.

approach.notes: A standard anti-Sicilian, like the Closed Sicilian. Played by strong players now and then.

level.notes: Plans are clear, but the right moment to push f4-f5 or hit back with ...d5 is a matter of judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: Black ...d5 at once
sublines_that_differ.how: Black challenges e4 immediately and play is more open.

character.reason: Manoeuvring with opposite-wing plans but little forcing play.

structure.reason: Sicilian asymmetric centre with the c-file for Black.
